title: Bitpacking & Eval Probes — Applied ML weekly digest (2026-05-28)
content:
Meeting: Applied ML weekly sync — focus on bitpacking experiments, eval probes, and onboarding steps for the new 13B open model.
Date: 2026-05-28
Attendees: Asha (owner), Luca, Maya, Noah, + async notes from Priya

TL;DR:
- Small wins on 4-bit bitpacking for dense FF layers: ~12% token-cost reduction in microbench harness; regressed on some open-book QA evals.
- Eval probes added to pipeline to catch hallucination spikes after quant/pack passes. Early findings: small increase in answer diversity but higher F1 variance on short-context tasks.
- Model onboarding checklist for open-13B drafted; next sprint: finalize tokenizers and KVM mapping, run long-context throughput sweep.

Notes / Discussion:
1) Bitpacking experiments (Luca)
- What we tried: custom bitpack layer that concatenates 2x4-bit packed values into 8-bit lanes to reduce memory movement. Run on R5 (A100-80) and dev-rt (A10).
- Perf summary (microbench):
  * baseline fp16 single-token throughput: 320 tokens/sec (A100-80)
  * 4-bit packed (no quant-aware-ops): 360 tokens/sec (+12.5%)
  * 4-bit packed + nightly kernel patch: 392 tokens/sec (+22.5%)
- Cost proxy (tokens/sec per GPU hour) improved ~18% overall after kernel patch.
- Correctness: RNG-consistent but small deltas in logits for tail tokens.
- Action: add a deterministic RNG seed run for 10k sequences and diff token-level logits to identify distributional drift (owner: Luca, due 2026-06-03).

2) Eval probe integration (Maya)
- Added three short probes to nightly eval: closed-book QA (TriviaQA short), summarization brevity test, and hallucination probe (synthetic factuality set).
- Findings: after naive bitpack + symmetric round-off, hallucination probe false-positive rate went from 6% -> 11% on the open-13B snapshot.
- Hypothesis: quantization introduces sharper logit peaks in small context cases; decoding heuristics (temperature, top-p) need retune.
- Quick mitigation tested: increase top-p by 0.02 and reduce temperature to 0.85 — hallucination FP dropped to 8% but diversity metric (self-BLEU) also reduced.
- Action: run eval grid for decoding parameters across 4-bit/8-bit variants (owner: Maya, due 2026-06-04).

3) Model onboarding checklist (Noah)
- Draft items completed: tokenizer canonicalization, initial model artifact ingest, basic smoke-run for inference correctness.
- Open items: KVM cache mapping for sparse attention blocks, prefix-cache priming policy, and long-context memory profiling.
- Risk: compiled kernel selection sometimes picks suboptimal GEMM for sequence length > 4096; causes 20-30% throughput drop. Need a fallback selector update.
- Action: profiling job to collect kernel selection traces across seq lengths 512/1024/2048/4096/8192 (owner: Noah, due 2026-06-02).

4) Sparse attention & packing interactions (Priya - async)
- Note: when sparse attention patterns are active, bitpacking increased memory fragmentation on A100-80. Suspect alignment padding interaction.
- Suggestion: add alignment-aware packer that respects attention block alignment boundaries. Prototype exists in branch 'align-packer' (linked PR).
- Action: test align-packer on sparse-attn workload (owner: Priya, collaborator: Luca, due 2026-06-05).

Experiment logs (quick capture):
- run/bitpack/v2/2026-05-26: seed=42, seq=1024, batch=8, tokens/s=372, sample_size=500, notes="tail-logit drift at token>900"
- run/bitpack/kernel-patch-1/2026-05-27: seed=42, seq=256, batch=12, tokens/s=392, sample_size=2000, notes="stable"
- run/eval-probes/2026-05-27: open-13B-snap-12, top-p=0.92,temp=0.9, halluc_fp=11%

Action items (clear owners):
- Luca: deterministic 10k-seq logit diff run and metric report (due 2026-06-03)
- Maya: decoding grid for 4/8-bit variants with eval probes (due 2026-06-04)
- Noah: kernel-selection profiling for long seqs (due 2026-06-02)
- Priya: align-packer sparse-attn test (due 2026-06-05)
- Asha (owner): consolidate results into onboarding playbook and send to console team for rollout checklist (due 2026-06-07)

Blockers / Concerns:
- Memory fragmentation observed on 80GB instances when switching between sparse/dense execution paths — could affect Dedicated customers using mixed workloads.
- Nightly regression alert threshold currently flags only +20% latency; need a second alarm for hallucination/F1 delta > 5%. (Action: ops alert tweak, owner: Asha, due 2026-06-01)

Notes to self (informal):
- Remember to check PR 324 for the kernel micro-optimizations; there was a nudge about 256-bit lane alignment that may be relevant.
- Consider adding targeted evals for short-answer extraction tasks — sensitive to quant noise.

Next meeting agenda (2026-06-04):
- Runthrough of deterministic logit diffs and whether drift is acceptable for canary rollout.
- Results from decoding grid (4-bit vs 8-bit).
- Kernel selector fallback plan and rollout timeline.

References / Links:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rl-infra/pull/324
- Confluence onboarding draft: CONFLUENCE-1234
- Jira epic for model onboarding: JIRA-ML-789

End of digest.

-- Asha
